A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KAN/MLP expressiveness and spectral-bias study. Their text, equations, figures and appendices are readable, and retained, revised and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on multifrequency wave regression, Gaussian random fields and solving the 1D Poisson equation, including learning curves and approximation errors.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results, revises the Gaussian-field training comparisons and adds 2D Poisson experiments with convergence curves and solution visualizations in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The B-spline KAN architecture, grid-extension technique and learning procedures remain unchanged. The revised KAN-to-MLP width bound changes the theoretical accounting of the representation construction, rather than introducing a new learning method.

E1.justification: Appendix A adds Poisson problems on the two-dimensional unit square with zero boundary conditions, extending the existing 1D PDE evaluation. The wave tasks and Gaussian-field coverage in dimensions 2, 3 and 4 remain.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 2 adds a cubic-ReLU comparator, labeled MLP_ReLU3, to the Gaussian-field training comparison. V1 Figure 3 compares only the standard MLP and KANs of different depths. The Gaussian-field test plots retain their original comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the reported Gaussian-field MLP configuration from six fixed layers to depth optimization, retaining width 256; the search procedure is unspecified. The new 2D PDE experiment uses a 101-by-101 sample grid, frequencies 2, 4 and 16, and 50 LBFGS iterations for its convergence plots. Existing wave and 1D PDE protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A and Figure 6 add qualitative solution-shape comparisons examining recovery of high-frequency structure at frequencies 4 and 16. Existing architecture comparisons and the Gaussian-field analysis of overfitting and tenfold sample increases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging the wave spectra over ten runs with different random phases. V2 introduces no additional run-count disclosures, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: The Gaussian-field training results are substantially revised between v1 Figure 3 and v2 Figure 2, including changed KAN trajectories and depth rankings, plus new cubic-ReLU results. Appendix A adds 2D convergence and solution-recovery findings favoring KANs. These are revised or additional results, not established same-setting improvements over v1; the wave, Gaussian-field test and 1D PDE plots are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.3 changes the required MLP width from (G+2k+1)W to (G+2k+1)W², and the stated parameter scaling from O(G²W²L) to O(G²W⁴L). Appendix C expands the proof to account for W² edge functions and potentially different spline grids. Section 3.2 also adds a restricted shallow-construction sharpness argument, substantially revising a central complexity result.

C1.justification: The introduction now confines uncertainty about the representation construction's optimality to the deep case, accompanying the added restricted sharpness claim. The principal claims about expressiveness, Sobolev approximation and reduced spectral bias otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3 newly qualifies parameter count as an imperfect measure for comparing architectures, and Section 3.2 distinguishes restricted shallow sharpness from unresolved deep optimality. Section 4.3 also reverses its practical recommendation for smooth functions from smaller to bigger KAN grids. Existing overfitting and shallow-theory limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A documents the new experiment's sampling grid, network widths and depths, optimizer and iteration budgets. Both versions specify pykan 0.2.5. Replacing the fixed Gaussian-field MLP depth with unspecified depth optimization reduces precision about that configuration; no search range is supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to He et al. (2018), Jacot et al. (2018) and Xu (2020). It also explicitly acknowledges Wang et al.'s previously cited empirical neural-tangent-kernel analysis and positions its spectral-bias contribution as addressing finite-width KANs, narrowing the earlier general gap statement.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. V2 adds localized explanations and remarks, adopts author-year citations, and reorganizes the appendices into the new 2D experiment, relocated increasing-amplitude wave figure, and proofs.

P2.justification: V2 adds two 2D PDE figures and revises the Gaussian-field training plots with another curve, changed colors and legends. V1 Figure 2 moves to Appendix B as Figure 7 without changing its plots. The ICLR template changes title, headings and headers, while the established single-column and multipanel layouts largely remain.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the representation argument by explicitly accounting for W² edge functions, acknowledges relevant prior spectral-bias work, and strengthens empirical support with cubic-ReLU comparisons and 2D PDE results. These gains are tempered by incomplete consistency and reporting: the abstract still describes only a grid-size parameter overhead despite Section 3.2's revised width dependence, and the new depth-selection procedure is unspecified.
